competitorFacts.text: ARC Prize named Tufa Labs and its Duck agent the first-place open-source solution for the June 2026 ARC-AGI-3 Milestone 1 prize.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Tufa Labs — Duck Harness technical overview
competitorFacts.text: Tufa Labs says its public Duck harness lets an LLM inspect game grids as image and text, write Python in a REPL, and keep context short by evicting older messages. This describes the published Milestone 1 system, not an unverified current submission.
Tufa Labs lists Dries Smit, Isaiah Pressman and Jeroen Cottaar among its AI researchers, with research interests spanning reinforcement learning, self-play and Bayesian methods.

discussionThreads.summary: Tong Hui Kang compares the three Milestone 2 winning ARC-AGI-3 solutions and links their notebooks and write-ups. He describes a shared Duck/TAAF foundation and compares serving, scheduling, context management and harness changes. In the replies, rellik13 says requests waited for cache space despite high decode throughput and describes reallocating memory to longer history. Mintu Kumar asks for request-latency and cache-wait measurements. The desk also read Franzen’s linked write-up, which distinguishes its submission configuration from inherited defaults and says the experiments were not a complete controlled ablation study.

socialPosts.author: OCEANVIN10
socialPosts.summary: OCEAN highlighted the Memento 3 preprint. Its authors report that a fixed language model revises an external rulebook and executable world model; on the 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, they report clearing every level with fewer actions than the human baseline. These are author-reported results on the public set.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A new ARC-AGI-3 research lead for the edition desk. The paper provides a concrete mechanism and results, but the public tutorial set cannot establish private-game performance.

socialPosts.author: mikeknoop
socialPosts.summary: Mike Knoop said the same thing is happening with ARC-AGI-3 while quoting Pedro Domingos’s comment that models are absorbing harness behavior. The quoted post links Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation. Knoop gives no named team, method, score or ARC experiment. The linked paper trains a proposer to revise executable harness code using feedback; its reported evaluations cover reasoning and multi-hop question answering, so the ARC-3 observation remains Knoop’s attributed comment.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Fresh ARC co-founder reaction for reporting on how models and harnesses divide the work. Useful research context, with no new verified Kaggle result or evidence that harnesses disappear.

socialPosts.whyItMatters: Recent ARC-AGI-3 community experiment; the author explicitly says one level proves little.

socialPosts.author: JFPuget
socialPosts.summary: Jean-François Puget warns that setting temperature to zero does not guarantee fully deterministic LLM inference. The post quotes a claim that temperature zero always produces the same answer. In a later reply he says the hiring wording should not be taken too seriously and was intended to draw attention to the topic.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Older catch-up lead for reporting on reproducibility and run-to-run variation. This is Puget’s general inference comment, not a measurement explaining any ARC leaderboard result. Preserve the clarification when using the hiring line.

dispatches.headline: Afternoon edition: ARC Slayers storms into seventh, with Keith Tyser on both boards

sections.heading: The Slayers make their move
sections.text: ARC Slayers is the big top-ten mover on ARC-AGI-3. Its 9.97-point gain puts it seventh at 41.19, up from 218th in the fresh past-day comparison. Keith Tyser is listed alongside dzjiann and mitubant. Those same three accounts also appear on ARC Raiders in ARC-AGI-2, where that team holds eighth at 62.08. Two contests, two top-ten entries, and a shared core of listed accounts. The rosters establish membership, not which person produced the score increase.

sections.heading: Chen leads while the gold places tighten
sections.text: Yi-Chia Chen remains first at 67.49, with Tufa Labs second at 56.52 and a 10.97-point gap between them. Son & Mark & Ronen is sixth at 41.97, just ahead of ARC Slayers, while NVARC3 is eighth at 40.97. The last of the 18 public gold places now requires 36.98. These are public-board positions; the private leaderboard decides final medals.

sections.heading: Franzen returns near the front
sections.text: Daniel Franzen is 24th at 35.86. The morning Wire reported his climb from 765th; the afternoon snapshot keeps him in the same place. Franzen was a 2024 ARC Prize champion and 2025 runner-up with the ARChitects. Farther down, Jingshui Fu is now 67th at 33.22, after the Wire caught the move out of a position below 3,500. The board offers more than one kind of story today: established winners returning near the front, and deep-board entries suddenly becoming contenders.

sections.heading: Memento 3 keeps the learning outside the weights
sections.text: The Memento 3 preprint is the research release to read alongside today’s standings. Its authors describe a fixed language model that revises an external rulebook, compiles it into an executable world model and checks updates against observed transitions before planning with them. They report clearing every level of all 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games with 44% of the human action count. OCEAN highlighted the paper on X. This is an author-reported result on the public games; it establishes neither a private-game result nor a Kaggle leaderboard score.

sections.heading: The harness debate has a fresh ARC-3 angle
sections.text: Mike Knoop said a similar shift was happening with ARC-AGI-3 while quoting Pedro Domingos’s reaction to Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation. That paper trains a proposer to revise executable harness code using feedback; its reported evaluations concern reasoning and multi-hop question answering. Knoop named no ARC team, method or score. In a separate public post, fshindo said the ARC-AGI-3 competition had taught them a great deal about harnesses and called contests a valuable learning opportunity. Both posts keep attention on the choices around the model, while supplying no explanation for ARC Slayers’ new score.
